recording: not recorded by the team runtime; self-recorded manifests under results/2026-11-13-range-bitpack/
protocol_reference: experiments/2026-11-12-gpusparse-u64-canonical/configs/protocol.json (context bundle, not on main); its timing reduction is reused, its baselines are not rerun here
question: What is the batch-1 latency of an exhaustive exact scorer over a range-split, bit-packed inverted index (Version A), and how large is its index?
hypothesis: The scorer returns the canonical top-k for every calibration query. Its latency relative to the published baselines is empirical; no speedup is promised.
contract: GSP-CAP32-U64-NUMERIC-TIES-v1: exact uint8 impacts, BMP float32/ceil cap-32 query weights, exact integer products and sums reported as uint64, every passage eligible including score zero, score descending then original numeric passage ID ascending

implementation.index: src/range_bitpack.h, built by src/range_bitpack_tool.cpp from hash-<N>.gsp
implementation.accumulator: uint32 in shared memory, widened to uint64 on output; start-up gate requires sum(query weights) * 255 * max term-document multiplicity < 2^32 - 1 for every query
implementation.selection: per-range local top-k (kernel 1), single-thread-block merge of ranges * k candidates (kernel 2)
deviations_from_written_spec: lookup_block is implicit: blocks are stored term-major and range-ascending, so a block's ID is its position in lookup_range
the carry between decode tiles is kept per thread from the shared warp totals instead of a shared carry cell, removing two barriers per tile
the block-wide prefix sum is a warp-shuffle scan plus shared warp totals
the overflow gate bound is 2^32 - 1 (not 2^32) because the top value marks slots already emitted by local selection
the gate and all query validation run once before the first query instead of per query inside the timed loop

inputs.split: 500 calibration queries only; the 6,480 held-out queries are not read

before_timing: tests/check_range_bitpack.py: independent GSP writer, Python oracle and Python RBP decoder; range sizes 1/3/64/4096; k 0/1/10/128; 32/256/1024 threads; empty queries, terms without postings, terms absent from a range, cross-range ties at the cutoff, partial last range, one-value blocks, maximal gaps, word-straddling values, repeated postings, largest supported score; eight guard rejections
100K and 1M documents, first 25 then all 500 calibration queries, k=10: in-driver comparison with exhaustive CPU scores and an independent file comparison with cpu_pilot score output
correctness.during_timing: every saved top-k group of every warm-up and measured round is compared with the cpu_pilot oracle after each process
correctness.rule: zero ordered-ID or score mismatch; any mismatch stops the run and is kept

timing.host: cuda5.cims.nyu.edu, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070, CUDA 12.6, nvcc -O3 -lineinfo -arch=sm_89 -std=c++17
timing.baselines_run: none in this session, by decision of the experiment owner
timing.process_order: three consecutive processes of the single variant
timing.boundary: host construction of the sparse (term, weight) list, query H2D, kernel 1, kernel 2, top-k D2H and event synchronisation; original IDs are produced on the device, so ID mapping is inside
timing.excluded: index build, load and upload; start-up validation and overflow gate; multiplicity scan; file writes; the CPU oracle and comparison
boundary_differences_from_baselines: the CSR drivers upload a dense per-vocabulary weight vector (about 115 KB); this scorer uploads only the query's (term, weight) pairs
the adapted monolithic path additionally pads the query and packs/decodes selection keys inside its boundary
timing.gpu_check: record nvidia-smi and compute processes before each process; do not start while another compute process is present
timing.stopping: all correctness before timing; no optional stopping; a technical failure is inspected, fixed, reviewed and rerun under a new run ID, at most three attempts

analysis.reduction: per process, the median wall latency of each query over the 20 measured rounds
analysis.primary: pooled median of the 1,500 query/process medians
analysis.also_reported: geometric mean of the 1,500 medians, per-process medians, quantiles, median GPU event span
analysis.uncertainty: 10,000-draw crossed query/process bootstrap 95% intervals, seed 20261113, conditional on this calibration set and session

exploratory_comparison.label: exploratory, different session, not paired
exploratory_comparison.source: pooled descriptive medians of run 20261112-cuda5-01 as published in the 2026-11-12 report
exploratory_comparison.limits: no paired ratio, interval or significance; different process session, possibly different GPU load, clocks and cache state

not_in_this_registration: range-size sweep, k=100/1000, kernel-time breakdown, rerun baselines, held-out queries; each needs its own registration
